title: Bronchiectasis flare-up (worse airway infection)

items: Bronchiectasis is a long-term widening of the airways. A flare-up (exacerbation) is a period of worse symptoms.
A flare is defined when 3 or more symptoms get worse for at least 48 hours and your doctor judges that treatment must change.
More cough, more sputum (mucus), a change in sputum colour or thickness.
More breathlessness, tiredness, or coughing up blood (haemoptysis) in some people.
Sputum culture at every flare, to guide antibiotic choice.
Chest X-ray if you have new symptoms or to check for complications.
Pulse oximetry, a finger probe that measures oxygen level.
Your doctor will choose antibiotics using your sputum result.
Ask your doctor about your airway clearance plan.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Keep up your usual airway clearance routine.
Keep a note of your sputum colour and breathing each day.
Tell your doctor when a flare starts, so your sputum can be tested.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Breathlessness that is getting worse or at rest
Coughing up blood in large amounts
Fever with chills or feeling very unwell
